label: alg:wedderburn-decomposition
title: Wedderburn decomposition $H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_\lambda M_{d_\lambda}(R)$
html:
Algorithm. Wedderburn decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_\lambda M_{d_\lambda}(R)

Algorithm (Wedderburn decomposition of H_n(q)). Decompose the Hecke algebra into its isotypic components indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n, yielding the Frobenius pairing \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda(q)\, \chi^\lambda used by Step 3.

Input

  • Braid index n \in \mathbb{N}_{\geq 1} and substrate parameter q \in R.

Output

  • List of pairs \{(\lambda, d_\lambda, y_\lambda(q))\}_{\lambda \vdash n} where d_\lambda = \dim_R V^\lambda (Hoefsmit-block dimension) and y_\lambda(q) is the Wenzl–Markov q-weight.

Algorithm

1. Enumerate partitions λ ⊢ n.
2. For each λ:
   a. Compute d_λ (Frobenius hook-length formula at q = 1, then
      q-deform via [hook]_q).
   b. Compute y_λ(q) via the Wenzl bridge
      (`prop:wenzl-bridge-applicability-qou`).
   c. Cache the Hoefsmit irrep ρ^λ on H_n(q).
3. Return the decomposition.

Correctness conditions

  1. prop:wedderburn-trace-identity gives the canonical sum \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda.
  2. prop:wenzl-bridge-applicability-qou asserts that the Wenzl bridge applies in the QOU setting, giving a closed-form recursion for y_\lambda(q).
  3. prop:wedderburn-as-noncomm-fourier establishes the algebra-level isomorphism as a non-commutative Fourier transform.
  4. The q=1 dimension of step 2a — the Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length formula d_\lambda = n!/\prod_{c} h_\lambda(c) — is machine-checked in Lean (QOU.Mathlib.numStandardYoungTableaux_mul_hookLengthProduct, sorry-free), so the block dimensions entering \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda are exact integers, not floating-point.

Complexity

O(p(n)) partitions, each requiring O(n^2) hook-length / cell products. For n \leq 9 (nucleon-scale): at most 30 partitions.

Python API entry point

from pyhecke import wedderburn_weight, partitions_of, partition_dimension

for lam in partitions_of(n):
    y_lam = wedderburn_weight(lam, q)
    d_lam = partition_dimension(lam)

The per-partition heavy lifting lives in the submodule pyhecke.wedderburn.

Witness contract

Canonical witness: wedderburn-lp-ew-wiring.witness.json. Records the per-partition (d_\lambda, y_\lambda(q)) table, the chosen q, and the upstream Hoefsmit cell-content table from prop:hoefsmit-ew-cell-content for cross-checking.

Notes

The Wedderburn decomposition is the most expensive step in the chain for n > 6, as y_\lambda(q) involves nested [k]_q factors. The native Rust core caches partitions across braid-trace calls.
